name: Validating AI in GxP Systems
blurb: GAMP, computer software assurance and risk based validation for AI.
title: Validating AI in GxP Systems
answer: Validation of AI builds on existing practice rather than replacing it. ISPE's GAMP guide on artificial intelligence extends GAMP 5 to AI, and the FDA's computer software assurance guidance moves validation toward risk based testing focused on what matters for product quality. The hard parts specific to AI are proving the training data is fit, testing on independent data and controlling model changes.

reading.body:
Validating AI in GxP systems extends existing GAMP and computer software assurance practice rather than replacing it, with the hard parts being training data fitness, independent testing, and model change control.

The pattern is continuity. ISPE's GAMP guide on artificial intelligence extends GAMP 5 and its data integrity guidance to AI systems, and the FDA's computer software assurance guidance, finalized in September 2025, moves validation toward risk based testing focused on what matters for product quality. Neither framework invents a separate regime for AI. The FDA's Quality Management System Regulation, effective February 2026 for device makers, sits alongside them as the quality system context these validations run inside.

For AI specifically, the difficulty is not the paperwork but three properties of models. Training data must be shown fit for purpose, which is a data provenance and integrity problem before it is a model problem. Testing must run on data the model never saw in training, which breaks the habit of validating a system against the same inputs it was built on. And every model change must fall under change control, which is awkward when retraining can alter behavior without any change to the surrounding software.

The data does not say how regulators will treat specific model architectures, what evidence thresholds will satisfy reviewers in practice, or how validation burden scales with model size. It covers guidance and effective dates, not enforcement outcomes.

sections.body: Scale validation effort to risk, test on data the model never saw in training, and put every model change under change control.

developments.text: ISPE published the GAMP Guide: Artificial Intelligence, extending GAMP 5 and its data integrity guidance to AI systems.
The FDA finalized its computer software assurance guidance for production and quality system software.
The FDA's Quality Management System Regulation, which incorporates ISO 13485, took effect for device makers.
